lessons: Keep hooks extremely concise and direct; the hook with the fewest words ('Movies in T.') achieved the highest 10% retention (1.0223) and start performance compared to longer narrative setups.
Avoid starting with long, multi-clause hypothetical scenarios or dense explanations, as seen in the T. rex bite and car crash videos which suffered very poor start performance (0.18 vs similar).
Eliminate repetitive phrasing and dense structural breakdowns early in the video, as heavy descriptive blocks trigger immediate drop-offs around the 10% to 23% marks.
Not enough data to determine specific patterns for the end of the videos since all samples show significant drop-offs and similar low ending performance relative to benchmarks.
worst_moment_types: Dense explanatory blocks detailing scientific processes or computer modeling (e.g., bone by bone, muscle by muscle breakdowns)
Long comparative descriptions involving heavy numbers and units of measurement without immediate visual payoff
best_hook_types: Short, punchy introductory fragments that immediately set up a provocative premise without overloading the viewer with setup
